title: VIBRANT VILLAGES PROGRAMME–II
body_text:
Central Government has approved Vibrant Villages Programme-I (VVP-I) as Centrally Sponsored Scheme on 15th February, 2023 for comprehensive development of select villages in 46 blocks abutting northern border in the States/UT of Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Ladakh (UT), Sikkim and Uttarakhand.
Central Government has approved Vibrant Villages Programme-II (VVP-II) as Central Sector Scheme on 02nd April, 2025 with a total outlay of ₹6839 crores till the Financial Year 2028-29 for the comprehensive development of 1954 select villages located in 334 blocks abutting the International Land Borders (ILBs) other than the northern border already covered under VVP-I in the States/UTs of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Jammu & Kashmir (UT), Ladakh (UT), Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Punjab, Rajasthan, Sikkim, Tripura, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal for addressing the unique and specific challenges warranting area-specific strategies.
2906 projects have been sanctioned under VVP-I by MHA and through convergence by Central Ministries/Departments. ₹959.66 crore has been released to States/UT under VVP-I till date.
A High-Powered Committee (HPC) under the chairmanship of the Cabinet Secretary, Home Secretary, Secretary (Border Management), Secretary (Expenditure) and Secretary of the concerned Ministry/Department as the members has been approved by Central Government to undertake relaxations in schematic guidelines of schemes of various ministries for effective implementation in border villages under VVP-II.
This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the the Rajya Sabha.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs informed the Rajya Sabha that Vibrant Villages Programme-I (VVP-I), approved in February 2023, covers 46 blocks along the northern border in five States/UTs, with 2,906 projects sanctioned and ₹959.66 crore released so far. Vibrant Villages Programme-II (VVP-II), approved in April 2025 as a Central Sector Scheme with a ₹6,839 crore outlay till FY2028-29, extends coverage to 1,954 villages in 334 blocks along other International Land Borders across 17 States/UTs. A High-Powered Committee chaired by the Cabinet Secretary has been constituted to relax scheme guidelines of various ministries for effective implementation in these border villages.
enrichment.context:
Vibrant Villages Programme was conceived to counter depopulation and lack of infrastructure in remote border villages, which had strategic and security implications given competing infrastructure build-up across India's borders, particularly the northern border with China. VVP-I focused on villages along the Line of Actual Control in Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Ladakh, Sikkim, and Uttarakhand, aiming to provide roads, housing, drinking water, electricity, mobile and internet connectivity, tourist centres, and multi-purpose centres to improve quality of life and check migration from border areas. The scheme is part of a broader shift in India's border management philosophy from a purely security-centric approach to one that also emphasises economic development and habitation as a means of border area management.

VVP-II broadens this vision to other international land borders (with Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Myanmar) covering a much larger set of states including Punjab, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, and the northeastern states, recognising that similar developmental deficits and strategic vulnerabilities exist along these borders too. The creation of a High-Powered Committee to allow relaxation of guidelines under various central schemes reflects the difficulty of applying standard scheme norms (e.g., population thresholds, unit costs) in sparsely populated, terrain-constrained border villages, and is aimed at enabling faster convergence of schemes like PMGSY, Saubhagya, and Jal Jeevan Mission in these areas.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Vibrant Villages Programme (VVP):
1. VVP-I was approved as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme covering villages along the northern border.
2. VVP-II was approved as a Central Sector Scheme covering villages along International Land Borders other than the northern border.
3. Both VVP-I and VVP-II cover the Union Territory of Ladakh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, VVP-I is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for northern border villages including Ladakh, while VVP-II is a Central Sector Scheme for other International Land Border villages, and it also lists Ladakh among its covered UTs. Hence all three statements are correct.

prelims_questions.question: The High-Powered Committee (HPC) constituted for effective implementation of Vibrant Villages Programme-II is chaired by which of the following?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that the High-Powered Committee is chaired by the Cabinet Secretary, with the Home Secretary, Secretary (Border Management), Secretary (Expenditure), and the concerned Ministry's Secretary as members.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the strategic and developmental rationale behind the Vibrant Villages Programme. How does border area development contribute to national security in India's border management strategy?

mains_questions.question: Examine the challenges in implementing centrally sponsored infrastructure schemes in remote, sparsely populated border villages. How can institutional mechanisms like a High-Powered Committee help address these challenges?
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 2 - Governance and Government Policies
